newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint ends weaker vs dlr, sterling futures plunge.
newsitem.headline: Forint ends weaker vs dlr, sterling futures plunge.

text.p: The forint closed weaker against the dollar on Wednesday after lively trade, especially in the morning, dealers said.
The Hungarian unit ended at 160.40/45, compared to an opening range of 159.70 to 160.00.
"It was a calmer afternoon after a pretty hectic morning," said Gabor Liener of Unicbank. "The afternoon fall was entirely due to a new surge in the dollar/mark on European markets."

The currency section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange saw another heavy day after Tuesday's record turnover. Total trade was 12.4 billion forints, with sterling and the dollar accounting for over half the turnover.
The dollar was mixed while sterling recorded large losses for March, June and next Decamber, with a 3.32 forint fall for next March exceeding the daily limit of 3.00 forints.

"Trading would have been suspended if the loss had accumulated earlier," said one dealer, adding that the high turnover was partly due to recent fluctuating overnight interest rates which have encouraged speculation.
Other traders said turbulent trends on the international spot market were being mirrored in currency futures.
